liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Casey Jones** (2 reviews): Upbeat Casey Jones with calliope-like organ in the background, strong Jerry guitar and a hip vocal; Early, raw Casey Jones, reportedly only the third time played, after June 22 [5][13]
- **Let Me In 83968** (2 reviews): Let Me In also sounds like an unfinished concept; Let Me In has left-channel hiss and other audio problems [4][9]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): During Cryptical you can hear why the band complained about the monitors [7]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One is called as good as it gets [8]
- **High Time** (1 review): Jerry sounds like he has something stuck in his throat while singing High Time [8]
- **King Bee** (1 review): King Bee is a highlight, with harmonica that gives the reviewer chills [6]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Notable for Bobby singing Dire Wolf [7]
- **Lovelight** (1 review): The last few minutes of Lovelight are the only listenable part of the rough final stretch [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Ol' Slewfoot**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- **Let Me In 83968**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd69-07-04.sbd.sirmick.remaster.29294.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 104 min; rated 3/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Fidelity is described as pretty good; Stereo recording with excellent mix until Doin' That Rag, then becomes very hard to listen to [6][9]
- **gd69-07-04.sbd.cotsman.4360.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 104 min; rated 2.25/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: First two-thirds is okay with some hiss and many cuts and splices; after Me & My Uncle it is very rough; Sound deteriorates badly later in the recording, which the reviewer finds a major drawback; Sound quality is good on Casey Jones [3][4][5]

## Around the show

- Played on July 4th, under two weeks before the American moon landing [9]
- Bobby-led show: after Hard To Handle, about 25 minutes of four country-flavored Weir numbers [13]
- A transitional show with early versions of future staples and a couple of songs that soon vanished [3]
- Show overall rated about average or slightly below [6]
- This was the first of only two performances of Let Me In [7]
- Summer 1969 had the band stretching songs like The Other One and Doin' That Rag with new sections [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-07-04.sbd.sirmick.remaster.29294.shnf**: source: sbd > mc > d >cd > shn > wav > shn [1]. Also: Soundboard source passed through mc, d, cd, shn and wav stages, then shn again; SHN by SirMick [1]
- **gd69-07-04.sbd.cotsman.4360.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
